why: The SDK is pinned in global.json (8.0.423) and the EF Core packages in Directory.Packages.props are
8.0.0. Without this manifest 'dotnet ef' resolves to whatever is installed GLOBALLY on the machine —
10.0.2 where this was written, two majors ahead of the model it was reading. The tool is now resolved
by the repository, so every machine and CI agent runs the same one.
PIN TO THE RUNTIME'S MAJOR VERSION. A patch bump inside 8 is routine maintenance; a major bump is the
defect this file exists to prevent, and it must follow an EF Core upgrade rather than lead one.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, stated because the task that created this file was raised believing it would:
scaffolding any migration in this repository emits six foreign-key operations against SubscriptionPlan's
owned collections — three DropForeignKey and three AddForeignKey, restoring Restrict in Up and setting
CASCADE in Down. That was diagnosed as tool-version skew and IT IS NOT. Pinning the tool was
demonstrated to produce a byte-identical diff. The cause is that PersistenceDbContext.OnModelCreating
sets DeleteBehavior.Restrict on every foreign key including ownership FKs, and the migrations snapshot
format cannot serialise a delete behaviour for an owned relationship — so rehydration implies Cascade
and the differ is correct. It is unrelated to this manifest and still open: see T-047.
'why' is not part of the tool-manifest schema; the reader ignores unknown properties, and JSON comments
are rejected outright. Verified by running 'dotnet tool restore' against both forms.
